metadata.title: fix(api): consolidate loopback RPC URLs and TLS verification into shared helper (#3543)
metadata.author: madhu-mohan-jaishankar

## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #3543

---

## 📝 Summary
This PR removes hardcoded loopback HTTP URLs and TLS verification flags and centralizes the decision based on runtime mode (SSL env) into a tiny helper.

Concretely:

Adds mcpgateway/utils/internal_http.py with:
internal_loopback_base_url() — returns "[http://127.0.0.1:{port}](http://127.0.0.1:%7Bport%7D/)" or "[https://127.0.0.1:{port}](https://127.0.0.1:%7Bport%7D/)" depending on SSL env.
internal_loopback_verify() — returns a boolean to use for HTTP client TLS verification (disabled for local HTTPS).
Replaces literal loopback URLs:
"[http://127.0.0.1:{settings.port}/rpc](http://127.0.0.1:%7Bsettings.port%7D/rpc)"
"[http://localhost:{settings.port}{settings.app_root_path}/rpc](http://localhost:%7Bsettings.port%7D%7Bsettings.app_root_path%7D/rpc)" with f"{internal_loopback_base_url()}/..." where used.
Replaces default httpx/ResilientHttpClient verification use with internal_loopback_verify() so local HTTPS with self-signed certs won't fail.
Updates one assertion in tests to assert against internal_loopback_base_url().
Adds unit tests for the new internal_http helpers.
Files changed:

Added: mcpgateway/utils/internal_http.py
Modified: mcpgateway/cache/session_registry.py
Modified: mcpgateway/main.py
Modified: mcpgateway/services/mcp_session_pool.py
Modified: mcpgateway/transports/streamablehttp_transport.py
Test changes: tests/unit/mcpgateway/cache/test_session_registry_coverage.py (assertion updated)
Added tests: tests/unit/mcpgateway/utils/test_internal_http.py
This is an internal refactor to remove hardcoded loopback scheme and verification; it does not change external APIs or RPC semantics.

comments.author: ja8zyjits
comments.body: Please add appropriate license docstring at the top of the file. You can copy from other files.

comments.author: ja8zyjits
comments.body: Why is this a separate Global variable? any specific reason for that?

comments.author: madhu-mohan-jaishankar
comments.body: "_SSL_TRUE_VALUES is not a global variable - it is a private module-level constant (note the _ prefix). It is defined at module scope intentionally so it is created once at import time rather than recreated on every function call.

comments.author: ja8zyjits
comments.body:
HI @madhu-mohan-jaishankar , 
- I dont see any value in having that defined outside. Specially when there is no reuse of the values anywhere else. In this case, it is just a variable with a default value with limited scope.
- Also we are not fetching it from any external configuration or environment.
- Might as well define it in the only function calling it `internal_loopback_base_url`

comments.author: madhu-mohan-jaishankar
comments.body:
Just to clarify - _SSL_TRUE_VALUES is not a hardcoded URL string or a simple default value. It's a module-level constant set used for membership testing (ssl_env in _SSL_TRUE_VALUES).

Keeping it at module level is intentional for a few reasons:
PEP 8 convention - constants belong at module level, not inside functions.
Built once - the set is constructed once at import time, not recreated on every function call.
Extensible - if we ever need to accept "1" or "yes" as valid SSL truthy values, we just update the set in one place.
The _ prefix already signals it's private to this module.

I believe the current placement is idiomatic Python.

commits.message:
fix: refactor internal_http helper and improve test coverage

- Extract _is_ssl_enabled() to avoid redundant URL construction in
  internal_loopback_verify()
- Replace _SSL_TRUE_VALUES set with direct string comparison matching
  gunicorn.config.py convention
- Add license header to test file
- Expand test coverage from 2 to 16 cases: SSL unset, empty string,
  whitespace, case variations, non-truthy values ("1", "yes")

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix: drop .strip() from SSL env check to match launcher semantics

gunicorn.config.py uses `.lower() == "true"` without stripping, and
the shell launchers use exact `[[ "${SSL}" == "true" ]]`. The previous
`.strip().lower()` would treat `SSL=" true "` as truthy while the
server actually starts plain HTTP, breaking loopback self-calls.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix: use exact case-sensitive SSL check matching shell launchers

run-gunicorn.sh and run-granian.sh use exact [[ "${SSL}" == "true" ]]
(case-sensitive). Dropping .lower() so _is_ssl_enabled() only matches
the exact value that actually enables TLS on the listener, preventing
HTTPS loopback calls against a plain HTTP server when SSL=TRUE/True.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
